frog_tax_man.//: Story Phase 6: the first recurring programme on the S.E.S. An original show: Franklin, a frog in a tie and glasses, is in trouble with his taxes. His accountant wears a green visor; the judge is a large frog in a wig. Crude green picture, rolling bar, an excessive laugh track, a dramatic sting for every tax term. Garrick is obsessed with it. Episodes are data: a channel carries the programme, a cutscene can play any episode on a vista's screen.
frog_tax_man.title: The Frog Tax Man

beats.line: announcer: THE FROG TAX MAN!
accountant: Franklin. Sit down. We need to talk about your return.
franklin: Is this about the lily pad?
accountant: You have depreciated this lily pad NINE TIMES.
franklin: It's a very old lily pad.
accountant: Franklin, you cannot claim forty-seven hundred flies as business expenses!
franklin: I ate them during work hours!
accountant: 'Pond maintenance.' Franklin, you live IN the pond.
franklin: Home office deduction.
accountant: And this canoe is not a 'mobile office'.
franklin: It has a DESK LAMP!
accountant: Two hundred and twelve dependants?
franklin: Tadpoles. They are all VERY dependent.
accountant: And the mosquito consultancy. Undeclared.
judge: Franklin. Did you itemize?
franklin: I TOOK THE STANDARD DEDUCTION!
judge: ...Case dismissed.
announcer: Next week on THE FROG TAX MAN: quarterly estimates!
announcer: THE FROG TAX MAN!
accountant: Franklin, it's the fifteenth. Where are your quarterly estimates?
franklin: I estimated them. Quarterly.
accountant: You estimated them at 'a lot of flies'.
judge: Is this true, Franklin?
franklin: ...Ribbit.
announcer: Remember to file! The Frog Tax Man!

episodes.//: Story Phase 7: season seventeen, the one Garrick has been waiting for. Franklin listed 27,000 flies as business inventory and ate them (business snacks or personal snacks?); his pond is down as investment property (Schedule POND); the dragonfly is a business expense (morale); no receipts, so the lily pad is forfeit; another letter: a refund (three flies); and then depreciation. All the forms are invented frog forms (RIB-40, Schedule POND, 10-FROG-X).

beats.line: announcer: THE FROG TAX MAN! Season seventeen!
accountant: Franklin. Sit down. It's about the flies.
accountant: Twenty-seven thousand flies. Listed as business inventory.
franklin: They're for the business.
accountant: You ATE them, Franklin.
franklin: ...During business hours.
accountant: So which is it? Business snacks, or personal snacks?
franklin: Can they be both?
accountant: Not on a Form RIB-40, they can't.
accountant: And the pond. You've listed your own pond as investment property.
franklin: I invest a lot of time in it.
accountant: That's Schedule POND, line nine. You'll have to file an amended return. A 10-FROG-X.
franklin: I also claimed the dragonfly. As a business expense.
accountant: What does the dragonfly DO, Franklin?
franklin: ...Morale.
announcer: Later that week...
franklin: A letter. From the Pond Revenue Service.
accountant: The flies, Franklin. Do you have the receipts?
franklin: ...Ribbit.
judge: No receipts? Then the lily pad is FORFEIT.
franklin: Not the LILY PAD!
announcer: And then... ANOTHER letter!
franklin: It's from the Pond Revenue Service. Again.
accountant: Open it, Franklin.
franklin: 'Dear Mister Franklin. Following review, you have overpaid. By three flies.'
accountant: A REFUND!
announcer: The Frog Tax Man will be right back, after a word from Pond Soap!
franklin: Can I have my lily pad back?
judge: No.
accountant: But you can DEPRECIATE it, Franklin. It's worth a little less every year.
franklin: So everything I own is slowly worth nothing?
accountant: That's depreciation, Franklin.
franklin: That's the saddest thing I've ever heard.
announcer: Keep your receipts! The Frog Tax Man!

episodes.//: Story Phase 8: the audit. A new character, the Auditor (a stern old toad with a magnifying glass). Four hundred flies filed as OFFICE REFRESHMENTS (eaten in the office does not make them office supplies); some reclassified as NETWORKING EXPENSES ("Were you networking?" "With the flies?"); receipts written on leaves; tadpole subcontractors. All invented frog paperwork.

beats.line: announcer: THE FROG TAX MAN! Tonight: THE AUDIT.
auditor: Mister Franklin. I'm from the Pond Revenue Service.
franklin: ...Nice to meet you?
auditor: Four hundred flies. Claimed as OFFICE REFRESHMENTS.
franklin: I ate them in the office.
auditor: Being eaten inside an office does not make a fly an office supply.
franklin: It made it an office fly.
auditor: Disallowed.
franklin: Then some of them were... networking expenses.
auditor: Were you networking, Franklin?
franklin: With the flies?
auditor: And these receipts. They're written on leaves.
franklin: We're a paperless pond.
auditor: And these, under SUBCONTRACTORS?
franklin: Tadpoles. They do the heavy lifting.
auditor: They're two days old.
franklin: They grow up so fast.
auditor: We'll continue this. After the break.
announcer: The Frog Tax Man will be right back, after a word from Pond Soap!

episodes.//: Story Phase 8, late at night (after everyone has given up on sleep): Franklin sold a lily pad for more than he paid for it. A capital gain. Taxable. "What was your basis?" "My what?" Invented frog paperwork, real arithmetic.

beats.line: announcer: THE FROG TAX MAN! The late repeat: CAPITAL GAINS.
franklin: I sold a lily pad! For more than I paid for it!
auditor: Congratulations. That's a capital gain.
franklin: ...Is that good?
auditor: It's taxable.
franklin: ...Is that good?
auditor: What was your basis, Franklin?
franklin: My what?
auditor: Your BASIS. What you paid for it. You'll need records.
franklin: I paid in flies.
auditor: How many flies?
franklin: ...I ate the records.
announcer: Can Franklin reconstruct his basis? Find out... next week!
announcer: Keep your receipts! The Frog Tax Man!

episodes.//: Story Phase 9: the excuse. Franklin's records were eaten by a shark, in a shark storm, and the Auditor does not care. Broadcast the morning the Revenge raises Crownskull Isle with the Great Sharkstorm behind it: a coincidence (the set doesn't know anything; the crew are not sure). Invented frog paperwork.

beats.line: announcer: THE FROG TAX MAN! Tonight: THE EXCUSE.
auditor: Mister Franklin. Your records. Where are they?
franklin: They were eaten.
auditor: Eaten.
franklin: By a SHARK. I was carrying them across the pond, and a shark came up and ate every leaf.
auditor: There are no sharks in a pond, Mister Franklin.
franklin: There are when there's a STORM.
auditor: A storm.
franklin: A SHARK storm! Sharks! In the sky! Going round and round! And one came down and ATE MY RECEIPTS!
auditor: ...
auditor: Mister Franklin. A sharkstorm is not a valid excuse for poor record-keeping.
franklin: It ATE them!
auditor: Then you should have kept copies. Disallowed.
announcer: The Frog Tax Man will be right back, after a word from Pond Soap!
